title: The Star's Hiccups
markdown:
In a room bathed in the softest moonlight, Bumble the bear and Pip the little puddle duckling were nestled ever so snugly in their warm nests, ready for a deep, peaceful slumber. Bumble’s fluff, a lovely shade of honey-brown, felt wonderfully warm and smelled faintly of meadowsweet and slumber. Beside him, Pip the fluffy yellow fellow was like a tiny, warm sunbeam, his little beak tucked neatly under his wing. They were just about to wander into lovely dreamland, with their eyelids feeling heavy as little stones, when… hic… hic… a funny little sound wafted from above.

Their special sleepy star, the one that lived just over their nests and wafted a gentle, sleepy shimmer all around, was hiccuping. Oh dear! It was a tiny, soft hiccup, more like a little sigh that tickled the air, but it made the star’s gentle light wobble and shimmer in a very odd way. Bumble’s large, warm, chocolate-drop eyes blinked open, and Pip’s little head popped up, his bright, curious eyes wide. “Oh no!” murmured Pip, his little voice barely a squeak. “Our lovely star is doing the funny hiccups!” Bumble’s low rumble, usually so deep and comforting, was very quiet, a soft rumble in his chest. “Poor little star,” he murmured. “Those little hiccups must be causing it to feel difficult to feel all quiet and peaceful, mustn’t they?” Hic! went the star again, a little fainter this time, as if it were attempting its most to be quiet.

Bumble and Pip gazed at each other, their soft faces awash with a soft, kind worry. They truly wished their star companion to feel well, so that the whole space could be filled with that lovely, sleepy feeling, and they could all wander off into sweet dreamland together. “Maybe,” murmured Pip, paddling a small bit closer to the side of the nest, his little webbed feet pattering softly on the carpet, “maybe if we hum it a very, very, very gentle tune, like the one Mother Duck hums to us, it will help it feel quiet and still once more.” Bumble bowed his large, soft head, his ears drooping just a little. So, together, in their softest, gentlest voices, they began to murmur a gentle, flowing melody. “Sleepy stars, sleepy skies, close your little sleepy eyes… moonlight soft and shadows deep, time for little ones to sleep…” Their murmuring was like a soft embrace being wrapped about the tiny star, a soothing sound in the hushed space.

Then, Pip recalled something else his Mother Duck often advised. “And sometimes,” he murmured gently, his small beak parting just a little, “a gentle breath helps when you feel… a bit ticklish, or like something’s making you twitch!” Bumble bowed once more, his large nose twitching gently. He drew a deep, gentle breath, and then, ever so softly, he wafted a gentle breath towards the light. It was like a sigh, hardly a stir in the breeze, and it carried the scent of clover.

And then, a lovely change occurred. The tiny star gave one last, silent sigh… then… quiet. The sighs ceased. The star’s light became steady once more, a lovely, peaceful shimmer that wafted a peaceful glow throughout the space. It seemed to hum with thanks, a quiet, gentle thank you to its lovely, kind companions. Bumble and Pip nestled back down into their warm nests, feeling so warm and content that they had helped their tiny star companion. The moonlight wafted in through the window, drawing silvery lines across the floor, and the peaceful shimmer of the calm light made the space feel safe and ever so cozy. A large, soft yawn escaped Bumble, a low rumble like faraway, sleepy rumble, followed by a little peep from Pip. Presently, both Bumble and Pip were fast asleep, dreaming lovely dreams, while their star glowed softly above them, keeping them safe until the morning sun arrived.
characters: Button the bear, Pip the pond duckling
